contract: CBWeb3 Scenario B — Hub-and-spoke settlement (quote and cross-currency swap)

vectors.title: Cross-currency quote — three parameters the upstream document does not declare
vectors.description: Generates a short-lived quote for a full cross-border settlement. Public: no credentials required.
vectors.notes: BLOCKING SPEC DIVERGENCE, mirrored to the implementation: the platform document declares ZERO parameters on this operation, while the handler requires source_currency, target_currency and amount_out and answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST without them (see swap-err-01). pool_pair and max_slippage_pct are genuinely optional; the handler defaults max_slippage_pct to 0.01. created_at and valid_until are UNIX SECONDS here, not RFC 3339 — unlike almost every other timestamp in this contract. THE QUOTE LIVES 15 SECONDS: issue the quote and the swap programmatically in one step. A fixture that pauses between them will flake.

vectors.title: Single-pair exact-output quote uses amount_out, not amountOut
vectors.description: The intra-Hub quote: how much input is needed to receive exactly amount_out on one pair.
vectors.notes: BLOCKING SPEC DIVERGENCE: the platform document names this parameter amountOut in camelCase; the delivered handler reads only amount_out. A client written strictly against the upstream document always gets 400 (see swap-err-02). Note also that this quote's timestamp IS RFC 3339, while the cross-currency quote's timestamps are Unix seconds — two conventions, same family.

vectors.title: Initiate the cross-border payment — the one call an integrator makes
vectors.description: Orchestrates bridge-in (the payer's Central Bank locks spoke tCeBM and mints its Hub W-token), Hub AMM swap, bridge-out (the BENEFICIARY's Central Bank burns and delivers on its spoke) and residue return. Returns a swap_id to poll.

preconditions.session: access_token COOKIE for the payer bank — this route is cookie-only
preconditions.reservePrelude: completed; payer holds at least max_amount_in of spoke tCeBM

vectors.notes: THE FULL max_amount_in IS BRIDGED IN, not amount_in — the realised input is unknown until the swap executes, so the whole slippage ceiling crosses to the Hub and the unspent part comes back as a separate RESIDUE leg. Size max_amount_in accordingly. Do NOT send payer_bank_id: it is deprecated and ignored, and the payer is derived from the session bankId claim. Observed status values are QUOTING, BRIDGE_IN_PROGRESS, SWAP_IN_PROGRESS, BRIDGE_OUT_PROGRESS, COMPLETED and FAILED; that vocabulary is not in the platform OpenAPI at all and is recovered from internal/domain, so the contract publishes it as a documented free string rather than an enum.

vectors.title: Poll to COMPLETED and verify SETTLEMENT, not just status
vectors.description: The assertion that makes this a settlement test rather than an API test. Poll until status is COMPLETED or FAILED, then check the money.
vectors.notes: Five settlement assertions, all of which a status-only test would miss. (1) The payer's tCeBM balance falls by amount_in, NOT by max_amount_in. (2) residue_amount equals max_amount_in minus amount_in. (3) residue_status is RETURNED — RETURN_FAILED means the payer has NOT been made whole and the buffer is stranded on the Hub swap signer. (4) The bridge-out position reaches BURNED or RELEASED. (5) GET /api/v2/amm/hub-reconciliation reports balanced true. Asserting status == COMPLETED alone is not conformance.

vectors.title: Swap history is scoped to the calling bank and is the only paginated endpoint
vectors.description: A bank can never list another bank's swaps and there is no parameter that would let it try — the scope comes from the session bankId claim.
vectors.notes: page_size above 100 is silently CLAMPED to 100, not rejected — a client that asks for 1000 and receives 100 has not hit the end of the data. Date bounds are YYYY-MM-DD and inclusive. A gateway with no history reader wired answers 501 with a body typed as SovereignSeedError, whose error_code vocabulary has nothing to do with swaps; treat 501 as a deployment-shape skip.

vectors.title: Single-pair exact-output swap on the Hub
vectors.description: The intra-Hub leg only: swap on one pair, receive exactly amount_out and spend at most max_amount_in. This is NOT the cross-border flow.

preconditions.session: cookie session carrying the commercial_bank realm role

vectors.notes: hub_sender_address is always a CENTRAL BANK address: the commercial bank never signs on the Hub itself. Do not send payer_id — deprecated and ignored, derived from the session bankId claim with a configured BANK_CODE fallback. The platform's shared 403 text on this operation claims it requires the CENTRAL_BANK role, which is wrong: the router gates it on commercial_bank.

vectors.title: Following the upstream document literally is a guaranteed 400
vectors.description: The cross-currency quote is documented with no parameters at all. Calling it that way always fails.
vectors.notes: This vector exists to be run against a live gateway and against a Prism mock served from the upstream document, because the two disagree: the mock will happily return a 200. The disagreement IS the finding. Verified in the delivered handler (internal/http/handlers/quote_handler.go:74-79).

vectors.title: Sending amountOut instead of amount_out is 400
vectors.description: The camelCase spelling the platform document declares is not read by any handler; the parameter is simply absent as far as the gateway is concerned.
vectors.notes: The delivered error message is 'pair and amount_out are required query parameters'. Assert the status and, if anything, error_code — never the sentence.

vectors.title: An unknown currency is 422 under a misleading error code
vectors.description: A currency pair with no registered corridor cannot be quoted. The handler reports it as insufficient pool liquidity because it collapses every quote-generation failure onto that one code.
vectors.notes: The code is hard-coded on this branch regardless of the real cause (quote_handler.go:90-94), so INSUFFICIENT_POOL_LIQUIDITY here can mean 'unknown currency', 'no corridor', 'pool empty' or a genuine liquidity shortfall. Do not build client logic that distinguishes them; verify the corridor exists with GET /api/v2/hub/currencies and GET /api/v2/amm/pairs before quoting.

vectors.title: A bearer token does not work on the swap routes
vectors.description: Twelve /api/v2 routes in Scenario B accept either a cookie or a bearer token. The two swap endpoints are NOT among them — they are cookie-only.

preconditions.session: a valid JWT presented as Authorization: Bearer, with NO access_token cookie

vectors.notes: The /api/v2 middleware fails closed when neither the session bankId claim nor the configured BANK_CODE fallback resolves a calling bank. The same 401 is returned for an empty jar. The bridge, liquidity, sovereign-add, token-approval and hub-reconciliation routes DO accept bearer — see amm_bridge_vectors.json.

vectors.title: Exceeding the daily transfer limit is 422
vectors.description: A Central Bank can cap a participant's daily outflow. The refusal is a business decision, not a malformed request.

preconditions.transferLimit: a limit exists for this participant and currency and is already exhausted

vectors.notes: 422 responses on this route carry a recommended_action string the other error shapes do not. No value moves: the limit is checked before the bridge-in leg.

vectors.title: Swapping against a pool that is not ACTIVE is 422
vectors.description: Pre-condition failure inside the orchestrator, before any value moves.
vectors.notes: Check GET /api/v2/amm/pool/{pair}/status first — it is public and free. An ACTIVE pair in the registry is not the same thing as an ACTIVE pool.

vectors.title: Swapping while the circuit breaker is halted is 422
vectors.description: Governance can halt a pair 1-of-N. Every swap on it is refused until two Central Banks sign a resume.
vectors.notes: Pair the pre-flight check in registry-hp-05 with this, and remember registry-edge-01: a status call that omits pair can report LIVE for a different pair entirely.

vectors.title: Omitting pool_pair is 400
vectors.description: Unlike the quote, the swap request requires an explicit pool_pair; it does not resolve one from the currency couple.
vectors.notes: Take the value from GET /api/v2/amm/pairs, or from the pool_pair field the quote echoes back. Never construct it.

vectors.title: Another bank's swap id is 404, not 403
vectors.description: Visibility scoping is expressed as absence: a swap belonging to a different bank simply does not exist as far as this session is concerned.
vectors.notes: Returning 404 rather than 403 avoids confirming that the identifier exists. The same 404 covers a genuinely unknown identifier, so a client cannot distinguish the two — which is the point.

vectors.title: An expired quote_id fails as a generic 500, with no distinct code
vectors.description: Supplying a quote_id older than its 15-second TTL fails the swap. There is no QUOTE_EXPIRED code: the failure falls through the handler's string-matching classifier to the generic branch.
vectors.notes: Verified: the orchestrator rejects the expired quote and marks the swap FAILED, and the handler's classifier matches none of its known substrings, so it returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR (cross_currency_swap_handler.go:307-312). 500 is declared on the operation. The swap record is created and marked FAILED before the rejection, so a 500 here is NOT a no-op — the swap_id exists and is pollable. quote_id is optional; omitting it skips this validation entirely.

vectors.title: A COMPLETED swap can still leave the payer short
vectors.description: The residue return is a separate bridge leg and can fail on its own. status COMPLETED with residue_status RETURN_FAILED means the payment was delivered but the payer's unspent slippage buffer is stranded on the Hub swap signer.
vectors.notes: This is why residue reconciliation must be asserted rather than status alone. Follow it with GET /api/v2/amm/hub-reconciliation, where the stranded value appears in unexplained and balanced reads false. The distinct BRIDGE_OUT_FAILED code on a 500 is the sibling case: the Hub swap SUCCEEDED and the beneficiary delivery did not, so it is never safe to blind-retry.
